decisions.reason: As a core extension of the firm’s established airfield systems business, this product fits the installed base well and is worth keeping because its strategic value is high and the option cost of continuing to offer it is likely modest.

This surveillance display strengthens the firm’s integrated airport-operations offering, and in a growing, R&D-active business it is sensible to keep the option open while surveillance demand and system-integration opportunities continue to develop.

The training program is complementary to the firm’s systems and services portfolio, and because service offerings are relatively cheap to maintain it is rational to retain it unless demand clearly proves weak.

This narrower training course looks easiest to discontinue or absorb into broader training services, and after several years it likely offers the least standalone upside relative to the managerial attention it consumes.

Airport collaboration software matches the firm’s stated direction toward real-time information sharing and collaborative decision-making, so it remains a strategically important option despite uncertainty in airport IT spending.

Because this multilateration system was presented as a flagship product and sits close to the firm’s future direction, management would be unlikely to abandon it before its full strategic and commercial potential is tested.
